summary: Hudson's platform series, beginning with its adaptation of the original Wonder Boy design.

entries.title: Adventure Island

emulation.notes: Use an owned cartridge dump, original 4:3 geometry, and integer scaling; avoid unverified widescreen patches.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Clean, low-latency rendering of the original NES/Famicom data.

primary.version: Original Hudson's Adventure Island cartridge release
primary.why: The NES/Famicom game is the series-defining version and the version reused for the later Famicom Mini and Virtual Console releases. Accurate emulation gives the cleanest practical capture without substituting the separate 2003 3D remake.
primary.how_to_play: Use a legally dumped NES/Famicom cartridge in a current accuracy-focused emulator. Preserve the original 4:3 image, use integer scaling where practical, and do not enable an unverified widescreen hack.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release and source for the later official emulated reissues.
all_releases.reason: primary: content-authority route with reliable modern emulation.
skip: an alternate original-era conversion, with no verified exclusive material that requires a second run.
skip for this entry: it is a remake rather than a faithful higher-resolution release of the original artwork.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld reissue of the NES game.
all_releases.reason: skip: portable official reissue, but a weaker capture route than desktop NES emulation.
skip: obsolete mobile route with no verified completeness advantage.

all_releases.platform: Game Boy Advance (Hudson Best Collection Vol. 6)

all_releases.reason: skip for the first game: useful compilation context, but not the best capture route.

all_releases.fidelity: Official emulated NES reissues on discontinued storefronts.
all_releases.reason: skip: no longer a clean purchase route and no content advantage over the original NES game.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The 2003 remake is visually newer but changes the presentation. It is not a fidelity-preserving replacement for the original NES artwork, and no sourced exclusive content makes it mandatory for this entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: Hudson Selection Vol. 4 is a separate 3D remake. The Wii and Wii U versions are emulated reissues from discontinued storefronts, not remasters.
